active_arc_audit: The filter contains zero because a(0)=0<=s. Its greatest index j satisfies a(j)<=s. Any later k with a(k)<=s would belong to the same filter and contradict maximality. Monotonicity is unnecessary for this selection lemma.
path_reversal_audit: Select the greatest active reverse index j. If j is last, s<=T=b(last) bounds the next endpoint. Otherwise maximality gives the strict next-start bound, using the castSucc/succ index identity.
The complement equation for b(j.succ) converts the next-endpoint bound to a(j.rev.castSucc)<=T-s.

For every k>j.rev, j=0 is impossible because j.rev is last. For j=i.succ, the off-event assumption excludes s=b(j.castSucc), turning the active lower bound into a strict inequality. Monotonicity of a and j.rev.succ<=k.castSucc then gives T-s<a(k.castSucc).
The path laws identify g(s) and f(T-s) on the selected arcs. The same reflected j indexes the stated barPost identity; no second reversal map or arbitrary state replacement enters.
R involutive and R(Phi_u(Rx))=Phi_-u(x) imply Phi_u(Rx)=R(Phi_-u(x)). Combining this with Phi_(u+v)=Phi_u composed with Phi_v yields the required operator order.
The remaining real identity is -(s-b(j.castSucc)) + (a(j.rev.succ)-a(j.rev.castSucc)) = T-s-a(j.rev.castSucc), exactly by the left complement equation.

endpoint_and_degenerate_audit.endpoints: The proof covers the entire closed interval whenever the stated off-event condition holds; no step assumes s is strictly between zero and T. In the actual strict-simplex discharge all event times lie strictly inside, so both endpoints satisfy that condition.
endpoint_and_degenerate_audit.n_zero: Fin(n+1) has one arc; later-index requirements and event exclusion are vacuous. Complement equations recover the endpoint bounds, and the same flow algebra applies.
endpoint_and_degenerate_audit.T_zero: For actual inputs with n=0 the argument covers the single point. With positive n, strict Prefix is empty. The generic lemma itself handles any supplied arrays and laws satisfying its premises.
endpoint_and_degenerate_audit.negative_T: No unspoken T>=0 premise: the generic conclusion has no s satisfying 0<=s<=T when T<0; actual T is NNReal.
endpoint_and_degenerate_audit.rank_norm_rate: X is arbitrary. No dimension, nonzero-normal, positive-rate or division hypothesis occurs. Those zero cases are not removed.
endpoint_and_degenerate_audit.non_strict_grids: Monotone a is sufficient; repeated grid values do not invalidate maximum selection. Event coincidences are excluded where necessary by the explicit hne premise.
